method.value: Numerically solve Poisson's equation for the finite-thickness gas disk using vcdisk; model stars with a spherical Sersic profile (or exponential disk + De Vaucouleurs bulge) and DM with an NFW profile; sample posterior probability distributions of partial (gas-only, stars-only) and complete (baryons-only, baryons+DM) mass models using MCMC; compare dynamical masses with CO, [C I], and SED estimates (including preliminary 22-point CIGALE fits)

evidence.quote: To determine the parameter values and uncertainties, we use a Markov-Chain-Monte-Carlo (MCMC) method to sample the posterior probabilities of the free parameters (see Appendix A for details).

The gas gravitational contribution (Vgas) is calculated by numerically solving the Poisson’s equation for a finite-thickness disk with a density profile ρ(R, z) = Σ(R)ξ(z), where Σ(R) is the radial surface density profile and ξ(z) is the vertical profile. To this aim, we use the vcdisk package1.
In the following, we compare our mass measurements with those from independent methods, finding some puzzling discrepancies.

claims.hypothesis: The cold molecular gas in PKS 0529-549 at z ≃ 2.6 forms a dynamically cold, rotation-supported disk.
claims.experiment: Performed 3D tilted-ring modeling with 3DBarolo on 0.18 arcsec resolution ALMA [C I] (2-1) data and applied asymmetric drift corrections.
claims.result: Measured a flat rotation curve out to 3.3 kpc, intrinsic velocity dispersion sigma_v = 47 +- 16 km s^-1, and V_rot / sigma_v = 6 +- 3, with negligible pressure support.
claims.finding: The molecular gas forms a regular, dynamically cold, rotation-supported disk despite the galaxy's extreme starburst and AGN activity.

evidence.quote: We find that (1) the molecular gas forms a rotation-supported disk with Vvrot/σv = 6 ± 3 and displays a flat rotation curve out to 3.3 kpc;
We find that the values of Vrot and the two versions of Vc are consistent within the errors, confirming that the rotation support is dominant while pressure support is nearly negligible.

claims.hypothesis: PKS 0529-549 exhibits non-circular gas motions in addition to regular disk rotation.
claims.experiment: Inspected channel maps, major-axis and off-axis PV diagrams, Renzograms, and the 3DBarolo residual moment-0 map.
claims.result: Detected a South-West tail (0.10 +- 0.01 Jy km s^-1, S/N > 3), an Eastern tail (0.030 +- 0.003 Jy km s^-1, S/N ~ 2-3), and a central blueshifted anomalous structure (0.20 +- 0.02 Jy km s^-1), totaling at least 12% of the [C I] (2-1) flux.
claims.finding: Regular rotation coexists with non-circular motions (two extended gas tails and an inner anomalous structure), possibly originating from a past major merger.

evidence.quote: The channel maps (Fig. 7) show that there are non-circular motions that cannot be reproduced by the rotating disk model: 1) a gas tail to the South-West of the rotating disk at line-of-sight (LoS) velocities from −191 to −88 km s−1 (SW-tail);
The non-circular motions are responsible for at least 12% of the total flux in the gas disk (2.8 ± 0.3 Jy km s−1).

claims.result: Gas-only model fails to fit the inner rotation curve; stars-only, baryons-only, and baryons+DM models all reproduce the flat rotation curve well.
claims.finding: A central mass concentration (stellar spheroid) is required, while strong disk-halo degeneracy leaves the dark matter halo unconstrained though consistent with LambdaCDM expectations.

why_this_data.value: Previous [C I] (2-1) observations had insufficient spatial resolution and sensitivity to measure the gas velocity dispersion, investigate non-circular motions, or construct multi-component mass models; [C I] lines are efficient H2 tracers in ALMA Band 4/6 at z ~ 2 where CO(J>=3) is weak and [C II] requires difficult high-frequency weather.

evidence.quote: For the same reasons, it was not possible to measure the gas velocity dispersion and to investigate possible non-circular motions in the molecular disk.
The [C i] lines are among the most efficient H2-tracers for galaxies at cosmic noon because they are accessible through ALMA band 4 and band 6.

why_this_method.value: 3D kinematic modeling with 3DBarolo fits a tilted-ring model convolved with the synthesized beam directly to the 3D data cube to overcome beam smearing effects.

evidence.quote: To overcome the beam smearing effect, various tools have been developed to fit a rotating disk model directly to the 3-dimensional (3D) emission-line cubes (e.g., Bouché et al. 2015; Di Teodoro & Fraternali 2015; Kamphuis et al. 2015).
The tilted-ring model is convolved with the telescope beam and then is iteratively compared with the observations to obtain the best-fit parameters.

alternatives_considered_or_rejected.value: Letting the kinematic center vary freely in 3DBarolo was rejected because disturbed kinematics on the approaching side shifted the best-fit center away from the kinematic minor axis.

evidence.quote: After several tests, we find that the kinematic center is difficult to measure because the best-fit value does not coincide with the kinematic minor axis (defined by the iso-velocity contour equal to Vsys) as expected for a rotating disk. This is likely due to the disturbed gas kinematics on the approaching side of the disk.

alternatives_considered_or_rejected.value: Using a radially varying velocity dispersion profile sigma_v(R) for the asymmetric drift correction was tested against a constant sigma_v = 47 km s^-1, and the constant value was adopted because both yielded consistent V_c(R) within errors.

evidence.quote: Fig. 6 shows the resulting Vc(R) assuming a constant σv = 47 km s−1 or a radially varying σv(R) (taken from the two-sides fitting). We find that the values of Vrot and the two versions of Vc are consistent within the errors, confirming that the rotation support is dominant while pressure support is nearly negligible. Hereafter, we use Vc from a radially constant σv for simplicity.

alternatives_considered_or_rejected.value: A two-component stellar model (exponential disk + De Vaucouleurs bulge) was tested as an alternative to the single spherical Sersic stellar model, yielding a slightly smaller total stellar mass (~8 x 10^10 M_sun) with strongly degenerate parameters.

evidence.quote: We have also explored a mass model (Fig. A.3) where the stellar component is given by the sum of an exponential disk and a De Vaucouleurs’ bulge (with n⋆,bul = 4). This multi-component mass model has four strongly degenerate parameters: the stellar masses and the effective radii of each component.

limitations_admitted.value: Strong disk-halo degeneracy prevents constraining the dark matter contribution without independent, high-precision (<25% uncertainty) baryonic mass measurements.

evidence.quote: The SED fittings, however, are not fully satisfactory, especially in the AGN-dominated far-infrared portion of the spectrum, so we will investigate this issue in more detail in a future paper, in which we will test different SED fitting codes and AGN models.

referee_caveats_inferred: The rotation curve is sampled by only 5 radial rings (width 0.09 arcsec, half the 0.18 arcsec beam), so adjacent rings are correlated and inner velocity gradients are heavily dependent on beam-smearing deconvolution.
Manual fixing of the kinematic center to lie along the kinematic minor axis could introduce systematic biases in the derived rotation curve asymmetry and residual moment-0 map.
If the gas disk is out of dynamical equilibrium following a recent merger (< 20 Myr vs orbital time ~ 80 Myr), circular velocities systematically underestimate the true dynamical mass.
